body:
`/hive https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` used to queue every open issue at once. It ignored GitHub sub-issues and issue dependencies, so with `--concurrency 4` on link-assistant/calculator it started the epic #227, foundation issue #229, and #233, which is blocked by #229, all at the same time. The CLI also rejected `/hive https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator/issues` (`URL type 'issues_list' is not supported`). The Telegram command already accepted that URL.

This PR makes hive queue only the **ready frontier**. An issue is ready when:
- it has no open "blocked by" issue;
- it has no open sub-issue;
- none of its ancestors has an open blocker outside that ancestor's own subtree.

A blocker counts as resolved only once it is closed, which normally means the pull request that solved it was merged. Ready issues all go into the queue at once, so `--concurrency` workers run in parallel. They are ordered critical path first: the issue with the longest chain of dependent work starts first, then the one that transitively unblocks the most issues, then `--issue-order`. Each worker checks relations again right before it starts an issue. If the issue gained a blocker since it was queued, the worker defers it to a later polling iteration instead of marking it done. With `--once`, hive polls again after the queue drains if issues were waiting and work completed, so `--once --auto-merge` walks the whole graph.

Relations are read with batched, aliased GraphQL: 25 issues per query, one query for all 19 calculator issues. The reader walks up the parent chain and keeps partial data on per-issue errors. Dependency cycles are reported with Tarjan SCC. If relations cannot be read at all, hive logs a warning and behaves as before (fail open). `--no-respect-issue-relations` restores the old behaviour. That suits repositories where a parent issue is meant to be solved as one combined PR. `/issues` and `/pulls` list URLs are now accepted as the repository.

Every GitHub relation type was reviewed:
- sub-issues and dependencies are used;
- tasklist `trackedIssues` are retired;
- `duplicateOf` issues are closed;
- linked PRs and branches are already covered by `--skip-issues-with-prs`, and an open PR keeps its blocker open;
- issue types, milestones, projects and timeline cross-references are not ordering relations.

The [case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2615-d911d7752514/docs/case-studies/issue-2615/README.md) has the requirements, the relation table, online research, the libraries and orchestrators reviewed (toposort, graphlib, dependency-graph, Forza, Sortie), the options considered and the calculator schedule. `IssueQueue` moved to `src/hive.issue-queue.lib.mjs` to keep `hive.mjs` under the line limit. `--respect-issue-relations` is documented in all four `docs/CONFIGURATION*` translations. Includes one minor changeset.

### Reproduction and validation

`node --test tests/hive-issue-relations-2615.test.mjs` has 19 tests. They use a snapshot of the real calculator graph ([data](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2615-d911d7752514/docs/case-studies/issue-2615/data/calculator-open-issues-relations.json)):
- the frontier is #229, #232, #231, #230, with #229 first; 15 issues wait, including #227 on 18 sub-issues;
- after #229 closes, six of its dependents become ready;
- a parent becomes ready only after its children close;
- inherited parent blockers apply, except blockers inside the parent's own subtree;
- also covered: cycles, fail-open, batching, partial GraphQL errors, worker re-check and deferral, `--once` rounds, and the `hive.mjs`/option wiring.

Live checks against GitHub:
- `node experiments/issue-2615-plan-live-repository.mjs link-assistant/calculator` gives the same plan ([output](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2615-d911d7752514/docs/case-studies/issue-2615/data/calculator-live-plan.txt)).
- The real `hive.mjs` was run with a stub `./solve.mjs` (`experiments/issue-2615-stub-solve.mjs`): `hive https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator/issues --once --all-issues --concurrency 4`. It started exactly #229–#232 in parallel, logged the 15 waiting issues with their reasons, polled once more and exited 0 ([log](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2615-d911d7752514/docs/case-studies/issue-2615/data/hive-once-calculator-stub-solver.log)).
- `experiments/issue-2615-calculator-waves.mjs` shows the 19 issues completing in 7 dependency waves ([output](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2615-d911d7752514/docs/case-studies/issue-2615/data/calculator-waves.txt)).

Local checks after merging main: ESLint, Prettier, the new suite, and the hive suites `test-hive`, `hive-extracted-modules-2175`, `test-hive-no-silent-failure`, `test-hive-solve-option-parity` and `test-issue-1718-hive-passthrough-false`. A full `npm test` run was stopped at 238/563 files with no failures when main was merged in. CI runs the complete suite.

### Remaining limits

- A blocker in another repository, or one hive does not pick up, still holds its dependents until someone closes it. This matches GitHub's "blocked" semantics.
- A blocker added while an issue is already being solved does not stop that run.
- GitHub Enterprise Server versions without these GraphQL fields fall back to the old behaviour with a warning.

Fixes #2615

title: feat(hive): respect sub-issue and dependency relations when queueing issues
